hypothesis: A small confidence residual trained on runtime-emitted controlled marker and distractor patches can improve their fixed-threshold decisions while limiting increased confidence on authenticated synthetic negatives.
isolated_change: Freeze the V37 model and geometry. Train its zero-initialized confidence residual using controlled-overlay binary cross entropy, an upward-shift penalty on synthetic component negatives, and a controlled-shift penalty.
training_split: The post-hoc exact-ink-deduplicated build partition: 194 emitted patches from ten user-authorized training study groups, with 98 inserted markers and 96 inserted distractors. Also use the identity-view synthetic component training negatives. Never label unmarked natural graph content as negative.
development_splits: A 24-patch exact-ink-disjoint internal diagnostic holdout from two groups; the fixed synthetic component and family development scenes; and the separate 16-project real development partition. Source-level overlap with synthetic development and image overlap with sealed real studies remain unverified.
metric: Marker precision and recall at the existing 0.1 operating threshold. Controlled-patch counts are conditional on proposal emission and are not scene-level accuracy.
limitations: The split is post-hoc, the overlay families are limited, the internal holdout has only two groups, 52 of 200 generated images had no proposal near the insertion, and manual annotations are imperfect. A successful experiment alone cannot approve a product model.
